summary: Volition's open-world crime-comedy series, including the original Stilwater games, the Steelport sequels, major standalone expansion, reboot, mobile tie-in, and released PSP prototype.

entries.title: Saints Row

emulation.notes: Use Xbox hardware/backward compatibility for the primary route; Xenia is a research option only if compatibility is verified for the exact build.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Xbox backward compatibility or original Xbox 360 output

primary.version: Xbox 360 release played on the newest compatible Xbox hardware
primary.why: The original Saints Row was an Xbox 360 exclusive; the best practical route is the original release through Xbox backward compatibility on modern Xbox hardware for cleaner output and convenience.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 release on Xbox Series X/S or Xbox One backward compatibility where available, or on original Xbox 360 hardware for strict preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster or PC port; do not conflate this 2006 game with the 2022 reboot of the same title.

entries.title: Saints Row 2
entries.definitive_edition: Windows with Juiced Patch and PC DLC-port route

emulation.emulator: None for primary; Xenia/RPCS3 optional for console-DLC preservation
emulation.notes: Use native Windows for the main run; emulate or use original consoles only for remaining console-DLC archival checks.

primary.version: Windows release with current PC fixes and DLC-port path
primary.why: Windows offers the highest fidelity and, with the current Juiced Patch/DLC-port route, can cover the formerly console-only single-player DLC content while retaining PC resolution and modding flexibility.
primary.how_to_play: Install the Windows version, apply current PC stability fixes, and add the Juiced Patch plus the Saints Row 2 PC DLC port for the single-player DLC; record the exact patch/mod versions.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original console DLC multiplayer-map components not yet covered by the PC single-player DLC port.
secondary.what_to_play: Only preserve or inspect the DLC multiplayer-map content if full DLC archival coverage matters.
secondary.why: The current PC DLC port focuses on single-player DLC components; the DLC's multiplayer parts are not the focus of the first PC port.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster; document mod compatibility because the DLC port requires specific patch/mod conditions.

entries.title: Saints Row 2 (mobile)

emulation.notes: Use a Java mobile emulator only after documenting the exact dump/device profile.

primary.why: This is a separate mobile tie-in, not a port of the console/PC game; the original J2ME mobile version is the only released route.
primary.how_to_play: Preserve and play the J2ME mobile build on compatible legacy hardware or a documented Java mobile emulator.

entries.remaster_caveats: Preservation depends on finding the correct carrier/device build; do not treat this as equivalent to Saints Row 2 proper.

entries.title: Saints Row: The Third
entries.definitive_edition: Saints Row: The Third Remastered on Windows

primary.why: The remaster is the highest-fidelity route, with remastered assets, improved lighting, and the major mission DLC content; Windows adds the most flexible settings and capture path.
primary.how_to_play: Play Saints Row: The Third Remastered on Windows, then document whether any original-version DLC-only unlock packs matter to the archive.

entries.remaster_caveats: Compare with the original PC Full Package if cosmetic/unlock DLC completeness matters; the primary recommendation is still the Windows remaster for fidelity.

entries.title: Saints Row IV

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows Re-Elected Edition at modern resolution/settings

primary.why: The Windows release was upgraded to Re-Elected Edition with all DLC and cross-store support, making it the most complete and configurable version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows Re-Elected Edition with all DLC installed; document storefront and patch version because the PC SKU changed over time.

entries.remaster_caveats: Australian/censored regional builds should be avoided for archival completeness.

entries.title: Saints Row: Gat out of Hell

primary.why: Gat out of Hell is a standalone Saints Row IV expansion; Windows is the highest-fidelity native route with the most flexible settings path.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows release, either standalone or alongside Saints Row IV: Re-Elected for context; document patch/storefront.

entries.remaster_caveats: Standalone expansion; not a replacement for Saints Row IV.

entries.title: Saints Row: Undercover

emulation.notes: Use PPSSPP for capture/upscaling, but document any emulator-specific issues because the build is unfinished.

primary.why: Undercover was cancelled in 2009 but a playable PSP prototype was released free in 2016; the only meaningful route is preserving that prototype on PSP hardware or PPSSPP.
primary.how_to_play: Use the released PSP prototype with PPSSPP or real PSP hardware, noting that it is unfinished and may crash or lack final content.

entries.remaster_caveats: Cancelled prototype, not a finished commercial release.

entries.title: Saints Row
entries.definitive_edition: Current Windows release with Expansion Pass

emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows current build at modern resolution/settings

primary.version: Current Windows release with Expansion Pass content
primary.why: The 2022 reboot shipped on Windows, PlayStation, Xbox, and Stadia; Windows is the highest-fidelity and most configurable route, and the Expansion Pass covers the major post-launch mission/content additions.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows release with the Expansion Pass/DLC installed; document whether using Steam or Epic and the final patch state.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not conflate the 2022 reboot with the 2006 Xbox 360 original of the same name; revisit only if ownership changes produce a new edition.
